claims.text: Nirmata reported about $29 token-only AI cost per merged PR on its own engineering organization, from 477 merged pull requests in one week using 30-day spend pro-rated.
Nirmata's $29 per merged PR figure is close to a $29 per merged PR figure that one other engineering team has published from its own token spend.
Waydev's worked example computes cost per merged PR as $200,000 divided by 19,200 merged PRs (8 per engineer per month), which equals $10.42.
Unblocked's illustrative worked example (not a customer result) gives a cost per merged PR of $500 with low context and $261 with high context, counting only PRs that survived the churn window.
Unblocked's controlled test found that better context cut tokens 42%, ran 27% faster, and used 64% fewer tool calls on the same prompt and model.

Unblocked defines cost per merged PR as fully-loaded AI cost (token spend, tool and seat spend, review time cost, rework cost) divided by PRs that merge and survive a churn window, e.g. two weeks without being reverted or substantially rewritten.
Nirmata proposes 'AI cost per accepted outcome': attributed AI spend divided by PRs that merged and were still standing two weeks later, read against quality and review-load guards.

Nirmata distinguishes token-only cost per accepted outcome, managed weekly and moved by model choice, routing, context discipline and coaching, from fully loaded cost that adds engineers' loaded cost.
Jellyfish has reported AI spend at roughly 2.5% of the marginal cost of a merged change.
Anthropic's Claude Code docs state the average enterprise cost is around $13 per developer per active day and $150-250 per developer per month, below $30 per active day for 90% of users.
By Unblocked's arithmetic, 300 engineers at $150-250 per month is $45,000 to $75,000 a month on one tool.
An April 2026 study of coding agents on SWE-bench Verified found input tokens, not output tokens, drive overall cost, and runs on the same task can differ by up to 30x in total tokens.
Gartner estimates agentic models need 5-30 times more tokens per task than a chat interaction, and that inference savings will not be fully passed on.
Unblocked recommends per-user spend reports, enforced caps where tools allow them, centrally set default model and effort, and shared codebase context so agents do not rediscover the same codebase.

Model routing sends each request to the cheapest capable model by task class, repository, developer preference within policy, or automatic fallback; the guard is to watch PR survival on cheaper routes.
Nirmata recommends routing that exhausts included subscription plan capacity first, then overflows to pooled provider credits or metered access, to reduce spend without reducing usage.

Nirmata argues cost attribution requires joining gateway-visible request data (tokens) with code-host data (PRs), and that routing all tools' model traffic through one gateway gives a single tool-agnostic unit; the FinOps Foundation recommends a proxy for attribution on tools billed to your own account.

LinearB recommends attributing AI spend to the owning team rather than individual PRs, because cost per PR is too noisy per PR; blended team cost per merged PR is read monthly against the team's own baseline.
LinearB says every usage key and agent account needs a named human owner (DRI); unowned spend sits in an unattributed bucket whose size is the first finding.
Per LinearB CTO Yishai Beeri, human-led PRs yield in the high 80s to low 90s percent merged, while fully agentic flows fall to around 30%.
An arXiv study (Sep 2025) found 83.8% of agent-assisted PRs eventually merged but only 54.9% merged unmodified.
Faros AI (Jun 2025) found high-AI teams merged 98% more PRs but PR review time rose 91% and PR size climbed 154%, with no measurable org-level DORA gain.

Dash0 computes cost from token counts using a maintained pricing catalog, and for flat-rate subscription users reports an estimated API-equivalent cost; cost per merged assisted PR needs a GitHub or GitLab integration.

DX's AI cost management report computes estimated cost per PR as total estimated cost divided by merged PRs (excluding bot-authored and deleted PRs), with spend estimated as credits consumed × cost per credit.
Apiiro prices its automated vulnerability fixes at on average $78 per vulnerability, benchmarked against human triage, fix and test hours.
